title: On-call and Incident Response: process, runbooks, rotations, and game days
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response practices for production services. It covers the incident lifecycle (detection, triage, mitigation, recovery, postmortem), runbook format and examples, on-call rotations and handoff rules, scheduled game days, and templates for status page and customer communications. It is intended for engineers, SREs, and support staff who participate in on-call duties or incident handling.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a consistent, reproducible process for handling incidents with clear ownership, measurable SLAs, and actionable postmortems to reduce recurrence.
- Scope: Applies to all production services managed by engineering and eng-sre teams (hosted API, dedicated pools, private deployments). Non-production incidents (staging/dev) should use equivalent practices but do not require customer-level communications.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection and alerting
   - Sources: Prometheus alerts, Redwood Console SLO monitors, automated health-checks, external reports (customer, sales), PagerDuty, and on-call Slack channels (#incidents).
   - Pager thresholds: P1 pager triggers for customer-impacting outages (SLO breach risk, major latency/100% error rate). P2 for partial degradation (increased error rate but degraded latency under SLO risk). P3 for non-urgent operational issues.
   - Required alert content: service name, severity, brief symptom, incident runbook link, pager URL, playbook owner.

2) Triage and ownership
   - First responder (initial pager) must: acknowledge within 5 minutes for P1, 15 minutes for P2.
   - Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
     - Confirm and reproduce the alert (is it real or noise?)
     - Identify impacted customers/regions/routes
     - Set temporary mitigation (rate limit, failover to fallback model) if applicable
     - Escalate to the service owner or on-call lead if unclear or cross-service.
   - Ownership model: the service owner (from service registry) owns the post-triage plan. Eng-SRE supports cross-cutting mitigations (DNS, network, cluster).

3) Mitigation and communication
   - Mitigation priorities: keep customers safe (fail closed or degrade gracefully), restore service, minimize blast radius.
   - Use runbooks (section below). If no applicable runbook exists, follow the generic mitigation steps: rotate traffic, scale up reserved capacity, rollback recent deploys, or enable read-only mode.
   - Internal comms: create an incident Slack channel (#inc-<service>-YYYYMMDD) and pin runbook and command snippets. Post triage summary to channel every 15-30 minutes until steady state.
   - External comms: update status.redwood.ai (see templates) at the start of mitigation for P1/P2 impacting customers. Notify Account/Success for affected enterprise customers.

4) Recovery and verification
   - Confirm defined SLOs are back within tolerance for two consecutive monitoring windows (default 5m windows x 2).
   - Run smoke tests and sample requests across regions.
   - If rollback or config change was used, schedule a plan to reintroduce change with canary and monitoring.

5) Post-incident actions
   - Create a postmortem within 72 hours (see template below).
   - Assign action items with owners and due dates in the postmortem.
   - Track and verify action completion in engineering board.

Runbook standards and template:
- Runbooks are short, actionable, and include: symptoms, detection queries, impact assessment, step-by-step mitigations, escalation contacts, rollback steps, and verification commands. Keep any required commands copy-pastable and include required run-as user/context.
- Location: store runbooks in confluence under the service directory and link from the service registry. Every production service must have a runbook for the top 3 P1 scenarios.

Runbook template (copyable):
---
Title: <service> - <incident class>
Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD
Owner: <primary on-call team / pager alias>
Severity: P1 | P2 | P3
Symptoms: short bullet list
Detection queries: (PromQL / log query examples)
Impact assessment: how to quickly estimate affected customers
Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  1. Command / step (include exact CLI or curl example)
  2. If step 1 fails, next step
Escalation contacts: names and PagerDuty aliases
Rollback plan: commands and safety checks
Recovery verification: smoke-test commands and success criteria
Notes / links: link to repo, dashboards, recent deploys
---

Example runbook excerpt (api-ingest-service - high error rate):
Symptoms:
- 500 responses from /v1/generate increasing from 0 -> 40% in 5m
Detection queries:
- PromQL: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="api-ingest",status=~"5.."}[1m])) by (instance)
Immediate mitigations:
1) Enable fallback model routing: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/route/fallback -d '{"service":"api-ingest","fallback":"small-1"}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
2) If fallback fails, scale up dedicated pool: ./tools/scale-pool --pool api-ingest --replicas 3
Escalation: @oncall-api (PagerDuty) then @eng-sre
Recovery verification:
- curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .status == "ok"
- Error rate < 1% for 10 minutes

Postmortem template (required for P1 & high-severity P2):
- Title: YYYY-MM-DD - <brief incident title>
- Summary: 2-3 sentence impact summary for readers
- Severity: P1/P2/P3
- Start / End times (UTC) and duration
- Timeline: ordered events with timestamps and owners (bullet list)
- Root cause analysis: technical root cause and contributing factors
- Impact: customer-facing impact and internal knock-on effects
- Mitigations applied during incident
- Corrective actions: list with owner and due date (must include at least one action that reduces detection/MTTA or recurrence risk)
- Follow-up: verification steps and when to close the action items
- Postmortem owner: name and team

On-call rotations and policies:
- Rotation model: weekly primary on-call per team with 2-week secondary (backfill) for major services. Rotations use PagerDuty with schedule published to the team calendar.
- Shift start: Monday 09:00 local timezone (team-specific) and ends the following Monday 09:00.
- Handoffs: out-going on-call must publish a short handoff note in the on-call Slack channel at least 30 minutes before shift end summarizing ongoing incidents, degraded features, and any maintenance windows.
- Time off and vacation: engineers must schedule swaps in PagerDuty at least 72 hours in advance; last-minute swaps require team lead approval.
- On-call compensation: per People Ops policy (see company handbook link).
- Secondary responsibilities: primary handles P1/P2; secondary handles escalations and longer-running incident coordination. If primary is saturated > 60 minutes, secondary must join incident channel.

Game days (simulated incidents):
- Frequency: quarterly for core platform services, biannual for lower-criticality services.
- Owners: eng-sre + service team. Each game day has an objectives doc and a short retro.
- Typical agenda (half day):
  1. Pre-brief (15m): scope, SLOs, safety rules
  2. Run simulation (60-90m): introduce alerts and observe response
  3. Post-run retro (30-45m): what worked, gaps, action items
  4. Follow-up: place corrective actions on the engineering board with owners and due dates
- Sample scenarios: sudden 5xx surge, KV cache poisoning, region outage, and control-plane latency spike.

Status page and customer communications templates:
- Use status.redwood.ai for customer-facing updates. For P1 and major P2 incidents provide: initial acknowledgement, periodic updates (every 30-60m), and a final resolution note with impact summary and follow-up.

Customer-facing status template (initial):
- Title: Investigating: <service> partial outage
- Impact: Customers in <region(s)> may experience increased errors or latency for <endpoints>.
- Status: Investigating
- Time detected: <UTC time>
- Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner
- Mitigation: Our engineering team is actively investigating and has applied temporary mitigations where possible.

Customer-facing status template (update):
- Title: Update: <service> - mitigation in progress
- Impact: Still occurring for X% of requests; primary affected endpoints: <list>.
- Status: Mitigating
- Actions taken: <short bullet list>
- Next update: in 30-60 minutes

Customer-facing status template (resolved):
- Title: Resolved: <service> outage
- Impact: Root cause & customer impact summary
- Status: Resolved
- Timeline and mitigation: brief timeline, actions taken, and any necessary customer-facing next steps (replay, re-ingest, config change)
- Follow-up: Postmortem will be published within 72 hours (link) or earlier if security-sensitive.

Internal incident Slack template (first post):
- Channel: #inc-<service>-YYYYMMDD
- Message:
  - Short title and severity
  - What happened (1-2 sentences)
  - Who is on call (primary, secondary)
  - Link to runbook, dashboards, pager URL
  - Immediate next step and owner

Operational tooling and dashboards:
- Required dashboards: per-route latency, error rate, token throughput, autoscaler metrics, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
- SLOs: per-service error-rate (99.9% success for critical endpoints) and p95/p99 latency targets defined in the service registry. Engineering teams must maintain runbook links on their dashboards.

Ownership and governance:
- Every service must have: a service owner, a documented runbook with top-3 P1 scenarios, an up-to-date PagerDuty schedule, and assigned on-call reviewers.
- Conformance reviews: eng-sre will audit runbook coverage quarterly and notify teams of gaps. Repeat non-conformance escalates to Engineering leadership.

Training and knowledge transfer:
- New on-call engineers: complete the on-call quickstart (eng-developer-experience/quickstarts) and shadow 2 shifts before primary duty.
- Game day participation counts as required training for on-call certification.

Measurement and continuous improvement:
- Key metrics tracked: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to restore (MTTR), number of repeat incidents by root cause, and postmortem action completion rate.
- Reporting cadence: monthly SRE review and quarterly executive summary for leadership with trends and major incidents.

Appendices:
A. Escalation matrix (example):
- On-call primary -> service owner -> eng-sre lead -> VP Eng (for >4 hour unresolved P1 impacting >10% of customers)
B. Contact list (replaceable aliases):
- PagerDuty: @oncall-api, @oncall-storage
- Slack: #eng-sre, #oncall-handoffs
- Emergency pager: +1-555-0100 (ops desk)
C. Example commands and snippets (sensitive tokens redacted):
- Health check: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .
- Scale pool: ./tools/scale-pool --pool api-ingest --replicas 3
- Fallback routing: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/route/fallback -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{"service":"api-ingest","fallback":"small-1"}'

Document maintenance:
- Owners must review this page annually or when a major process or tool changes.
- To propose edits, create a pull request against the confluence doc or contact the page owner.
